package_info.package_name: JFrog Xray SIEM Plugin for Splunk
package_info.package_versions: Initial release (2021-05, as shown in logs)
package_info.why_malicious: Not malicious. This package is a security integration tool designed to forward vulnerability and license compliance data from JFrog Xray to Splunk SIEM for enhanced DevSecOps visibility and response. No evidence of malicious code, suspicious behavior, or indicators of compromise is present in the report. All observed behaviors align with the intended functionality of a SIEM integration.

behavioral_signatures: Real-time forwarding of vulnerability and license compliance events from JFrog Xray to Splunk, matching expected integration behavior.
Mapping of Xray data to Splunk’s Common Information Model (CIM) for standardized event representation.
Dashboard visualization of security and license violations, impacted artifacts, and components within Splunk, as expected for this integration.
file_indicators: No suspicious file patterns detected; expected files include Splunk dashboard configuration files (e.g., .xml, .conf) and Xray event log files.
network_indicators: API calls to JFrog Xray endpoints (e.g., /xray/api/v1/violations) for event retrieval.
Internal communication between JFrog Xray and Splunk Enterprise over secure channels (HTTPS), with no evidence of unexpected external network connections.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for API calls from the JFrog Xray SIEM Plugin to Splunk and verify that all data mappings conform to Splunk’s CIM. No malicious activity is expected; investigate any unexpected outbound network connections, file modifications outside the described integration scope, or deviations from documented event flows. Automated detection systems should baseline normal plugin behavior and alert on anomalies such as unauthorized data exfiltration, creation of unexpected files, or communication with unapproved external endpoints.
